extracted.intended_audience: UK companies, business owners, finance directors, and tax advisers considering or preparing a Patent Box claim
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for UK companies on determining eligibility for the Patent Box regime and calculating the taxable profits eligible for the effective 10% corporation tax rate, including interaction with R&D tax relief and election timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying company & exploited patented inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for Patent Box, a company liable to UK corporation tax must make profits from exploiting qualifying patented inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A product may only need one patented component for all its revenue to fall within the regime (eg if one component of a car is patented, it may be possible for the total taxable profits from the sale of the car to be brought into the Patent Box regime). Patent Box can also be claimed on processes (and not just products/innovations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying patents and accepted granting authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies owning qualifying patents (or holding exclusive licences for those patents) granted by the IPO, the European Patent Office or other certain European patent offices will meet the first condition for eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusive licences count. If you’ve applied for a patent that is expected to be profitable but it’s not yet been granted, the benefit can still apply; however, the related relief will be provided in the period the patent is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company involvement in development/innovation (nexus requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: In all cases, the company must be involved in the development/innovation of the qualifying IP rights or products incorporating the patented invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement supports the policy nexus between taxable profits and the R&D/innovation activities that generated the IP; companies should assess and document their role in developing the qualifying IP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying relevant IP taxable profits (streaming requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Taxable profits arising from patented technology must be identified and streamed so only qualifying IP profits receive the Patent Box benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant taxable profits may include income and expenditure relating to patent licensing and royalties, patents used in processes or services, damages, infringement income and patent rights sold. The majority of taxable profits will be generated from products or parts of a product covered by the patent. HMRC has provided detailed guidance on how to stream qualifying IP income.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove the routine return
rubrics_metrics.description: The calculation must remove the profit a business might be expected to make if it did not have access to IP or other intangible assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This step aims to isolate the excess profit attributable to the patent beyond the ordinary returns to the business; companies must apply the prescribed method to strip out routine returns before applying the Patent Box rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove the Marketing Asset Return (MAR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The calculation must remove the arm’s length element of profit that relates to the company’s brand and marketing assets (the MAR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For companies which trade business-to-business (B2B), the MAR may be zero. The MAR removal ensures profits attributable to marketing/brand are not inappropriately included in Patent Box-eligible profits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculate the R&D fraction (nexus-based limitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: An R&D fraction limits the level of profits eligible for the effective 10% regime depending on the level of R&D work undertaken in-house or subcontracted and amounts paid for the IP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This step requires companies to track and trace R&D expenditure relating to the development of a particular qualifying IP right, including distinguishing between in-house and subcontracted work and payments for externally acquired IP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism of relief and tax computation
rubrics_metrics.description: The effective 10% tax rate is given by an additional deduction within the corporation tax computation, reducing taxable trading profits or creating/increasing taxable losses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This deduction reduces corporation tax liabilities (giving an effective 10% rate on qualifying profits) but, unlike R&D tax credits, it cannot be exchanged for a cash repayment. Resulting losses can be used to offset other periods or group companies' taxable profits subject to normal rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with R&D tax reliefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Box complements the R&D tax relief regime and companies should consider claiming under both where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two regimes interact and can be optimised together; companies often work on R&D claims and Patent Box calculations in tandem to maximise overall tax relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election timing and advisory support
rubrics_metrics.description: Selecting the most advantageous time to elect into the Patent Box regime is important and companies should seek specialist advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners (tax advisers and patent attorneys) can help determine timing, eligibility, and the best approach to make an election, as well as assist with documentation and liaising with HMRC. Saffery recommends working with advisers to optimise the business’ R&D tax credit relief alongside Patent Box benefits.
